item.title: Druski Delivers SNL’s Biggest Audience In Two Years
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Druski's SNL hosting debut drew 5.6 million TV viewers, giving the show its largest audience since November 2024.
item.content:encoded:
Druski brought 5.6 million television viewers to Saturday Night Live and gave the show its biggest audience in two years. His November 7 hosting debut paired the comedian with musical guest The Strokes.

LateNighter reported the Nielsen Live+Same Day figures from ratings data it licenses independently. The episode attracted roughly 1.5 million adults ages 18 to 49, with total viewership rising 8 percent over the previous week’s broadcast.

That last episode featured host Inde Navarrette and musical guest Gracie Abrams. Druski’s installment also improved 18 percent among viewers ages 18 to 49, giving NBC a stronger showing in that advertising demographic.

The comparison stretches back to November 2, 2024, when John Mulaney hosted alongside Chappell Roan and Kamala Harris made a surprise appearance. That broadcast pulled 6.8 million viewers, a mark Druski’s episode did not surpass.

Those new figures cover television viewing only and do not include live Peacock streams or social media traffic. Additional delayed-viewing numbers were not yet available in LateNighter’s initial ratings report.

The result adds a measurable television win to a busy stretch for the creator behind Coulda Been Records. As AllHipHop previously reported, Druski recently secured a multiyear Netflix agreement through his company 4Lifers, expanding beyond the internet platforms where he built his audience.

That arrangement brings his existing comedy franchises to Netflix while also creating room for original projects. The licensed titles include Coulda Been Love, Coulda Been Daddy and Coulda Been Records Auditions, rather than just a single stand-up special or one newly commissioned series. His existing series and sketches have generated more than one billion combined YouTube views, according to the agreement details AllHipHop reported earlier this month.

His SNL appearance gave viewers another look at the character work powering that business. The debut included a “Dru Can See Everything” sketch involving Elizabeth Holmes, while Emma Stone appeared during his opening monologue.

Netflix’s upcoming slate also includes Collect & Praise, a comedy built around Druski playing a money-hungry pastor. Mike Epps appears opposite him as a deacon in the project, extending that character-based format beyond his online sketches.

Collect & Praise is slated to arrive on Netflix on December 1.

item.title: Dreamville Organizers Seek April 2027 Return To Dix Park
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Dreamville organizers file paperwork for a potential festival successor as Raleigh waits for its next big rap gathering.
item.content:encoded:
J. Cole‘s Dreamville organizers have filed permits for a possible successor festival in Raleigh, with the application proposing April 3-4, 2027, and city approval pending, according to WRAL.

That puts fresh movement behind a question Raleigh has been living with since Dreamville’s farewell. The city and ScoreMore already have an agreement allowing April festivals through 2029, but it doesn’t require organizers to stage one every year. WRAL obtained that agreement earlier this year.

The promise of another festival goes back to April 2025, when Dreamville’s team joined city officials to discuss what would follow the final edition.

Raleigh Parks Director Stephen Bentley described the partnership in the city’s announcement: “It really does take a village. It takes all of us working together to build something that’s unique.”

That last Dreamville weekend left a big stage to fill in North Carolina. As AllHipHop previously reported, Cole brought Erykah Badu out during his closing set to perform “Too Deep for the Intro.”

Lil Wayne’s appearance reunited the Hot Boys and Big Tymers, while the bill also included 21 Savage, Tems, GloRilla, J.I.D. and Ari Lennox.

Cole addressed the workload behind the event during that finale and said the festival’s community spirit would survive a branding change. The city described the original gathering as a collaboration between Dreamville and ScoreMore Shows, a Live Nation subsidiary.

The city said previous editions attracted more than 100,000 total guests, with 2024 drawing visitors from all 50 states and multiple countries.

The empty spring weekend hit local businesses this year. In WRAL’s April coverage, The Big Easy manager Courtney McGlone predicted a substantial sales hit: “I can at least guarantee there’s going to be a 30% deficit.” The station also spoke with local retailers who wanted the crowds back.

The financial stakes go beyond the stage and the festival gates. WRAL reported that the 2024 event generated $145.9 million in economic impact for Raleigh, while the city’s agreement allows a future festival to sell up to 52,500 tickets.

The agreement sets the city’s annual fee at $125,000 for one festival or $225,000 for two consecutive festivals.

item.title: Ja Rule Books Two Performances For Ravens-Chargers Monday Night Game
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Ja Rule is booked for pregame and halftime sets when the Ravens host the Chargers in Baltimore on November 16.
item.content:encoded:
Ja Rule is giving Baltimore fans two chances to catch him when the Ravens face Los Angeles on Monday night. The rapper is booked for a pregame set and a halftime performance during the November 16 matchup.

The first performance is scheduled for 6:45 P.M. at the Bud Light Talon, giving fans an early start before the game begins. He’ll then perform inside M&T Bank Stadium at halftime, according to an announcement on the Ravens’ official Instagram account.

Baltimore hosts the Los Angeles Chargers with kickoff scheduled for 8:15 P.M. Eastern on ESPN. That puts Ja Rule’s first set 90 minutes before kickoff, with the second appearance coming after the opening two quarters.

The Ravens’ appearance comes amid a run of new ventures, including an overseas concert booking and a business leadership role. AllHipHop previously covered plans for his first Israel performance, announced for October 29 at Amphimax in Rishon Lezion.

Away from the stage, he’s taken a seat at IPX’s table as president of its celebrity board of advisors and a founding shareholder. The company says he’ll help shape financing and production arrangements that let creators keep their rights.

IPX pitches tools for producing shows, securing sponsors and getting projects to audiences through one platform. Its ambitions reach beyond music into film, television and livestreaming, giving Ja Rule another business to develop alongside his performance schedule.

“I’m a creative first, and I’ve seen firsthand what can happen to artists who don’t own their work. When I create IP, I make sure every show is my IP, on purpose, so that content will be ours, forever,” Ja Rule said in the company’s announcement.

“That’s why IPX is a game-changer for the industry, empowering celebrities, creatives and fans alike. We’re rewriting the script on how celebrities own and retain their IP,” Ja Rule added.

The booking adds another live date for a rapper who recently reconsidered slowing down his career. His catalog includes “Always On Time,” “Mesmerize” and “Livin’ It Up,” though those titles haven’t been confirmed for Monday’s performances.

IPX announced Ja Rule’s appointment on October 27, less than three weeks before his Baltimore booking.

item.title: RZA Invests In New Tech Company AYO Music Group To Track Down Unpaid Royalties
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: RZA puts cash behind AYO Music Group as the company searches music catalogs for royalty payments their creators missed.
item.content:encoded:
RZA is backing a company chasing royalty checks that music creators should already be collecting.

The Wu-Tang Clan founder has invested in AYO Music Group, joining a business focused on finding income lost in copyright paperwork.

AYO announced the investment, with RZA describing payment problems he has watched throughout his career.

The names behind that mission already have plenty of Hip-Hop history. Disturbing Tha Peace co-founders Chaka Zulu and Jeff Dixon are also among the investors, alongside family office CIH Group.

Co-founder Deborah Mannis-Gardner started DMG Clearances in 1996 and helped clear samples for Drake, Kendrick Lamar and Beyoncé, while Pär Almqvist co-founded sample-licensing platform Tracklib.

Mannis-Gardner also helped prepare De La Soul’s catalog for its long-awaited streaming arrival in 2023. At AYO, the work reaches publishing, neighboring rights and recordings worldwide, giving songwriters, performers and recording owners several places to look for missing money.

“I have spent thirty years making sure the people who created the music got paid for it, and I have watched a lot of money disappear into paperwork along the way. Deborah and Pär have built something that actually finds it. That is a mission I want to be part of,” said RZA.

One of its tools, Gapfinder, searches for registration problems that can interfere with royalty collection.

AYO says its database covers more than 57 million compositions and 210 million registrations across 300 international performing rights organizations, tracking duplicate entries, missing registrations and conflicting identifiers.

The service offers one-off checks of a writer or catalog, as well as subscriptions for ongoing access to its data.

That makes the investment another chapter in RZA’s dealings with the business behind the records.

Wu-Tang Productions previously struck a global publishing administration agreement with Downtown Music covering the group’s interests in its back catalog and selected individual members’ work.

That agreement included material from Enter The Wu-Tang: 36 Chambers, Wu-Tang Forever, The W and Iron Flag.

AYO remains invitation-only, with its business built around managing existing rights and collecting money those rights generate.

Ewing Athletics owner David Goldberg was AYO’s first investor when the company was founded.

item.title: Daddy Yankee Takes La Postal To TikTok In SoundOn's Biggest Artist Deal
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Daddy Yankee and SoundOn expand the La Postal rollout with TikTok challenges, an album hub and a Times Square billboard.
item.content:encoded:
Daddy Yankee‘s latest album is getting a TikTok rollout that reaches from phone screens to a Times Square billboard.

TikTok announced that La Postal is part of what the company calls SoundOn’s biggest artist partnership yet. The agreement puts its distribution platform behind the album’s worldwide delivery, artist services and promotion.

Daddy Yankee described the music through the relationships running across its songs, rather than the business arrangement behind them.

“Because in love, you find it all… kisses that make you fall in love, loves that betray, goodbyes that hurt, and hearts that learn to dance again. Some steal your heart, others your patience… and some teach you to love yourself first!” Daddy Yankee said.

The 15-track project arrived October 30 through DY Records, with Cardi B, Myke Towers, Danny Ocean, Bizarrap and Diljit Dosanjh among its collaborators. This announcement adds details about the business and promotional push behind a record that’s already out.

“It’s an enormous privilege for SoundOn to support the release of La Postal and help bring this brilliant new chapter in Daddy Yankee’s career to fans around the world,” Gabo Llano, SoundOn’s head of A&R Americas at TikTok, said in the announcement. “This is SoundOn’s biggest artist partnership to date, and we couldn’t be more excited to work once again with Daddy Yankee on La Postal and for the long term.”

Inside TikTok, listeners can complete tasks to unlock an album profile frame and challenges to access an exclusive Daddy Yankee video.

A search feature and dedicated album hub also let users explore the project. Users can find the experience by entering Daddy Yankee’s name into TikTok’s search bar, with the campaign already available inside the app.

“In the end, we all have a story to tell and a postcard we never sent. Because sometimes love brings tears, sometimes it calls for celebration… but it’s always something you dance to!” Daddy Yankee continued.

The Puerto Rican star recently credited Biggie as one of his musical influences during a Track Star interview.

Daddy Yankee will also receive the Latin Recording Academy’s 2026 Person of the Year honor this November.

item.title: Snoop Dogg's Swansea Club Eyes Stadium Growth As CEO Defends Spending
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Snoop Dogg's soccer investment enters a new phase as Swansea weighs stadium expansion and prepares for another Wales visit.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg could have more seats to fill at Swansea City as his club weighs expanding its stadium. Chief executive Tom Gorringe is outlining that ambition while insisting the team’s spending remains within football’s financial rules.

The club is working toward buying Swansea.com Stadium, Gorringe said in a BBC Sport interview published November 11.

New LED displays and a South Stand fan zone are nearer-term projects, with expansion of the 21,000-seat ground a longer-term possibility.

“We have to be aspirational and ambitious,” Gorringe told BBC Sport about the stadium’s future. He also addressed transfer spending: “We operate within the headroom of the financial rules,” Gorringe said.

Snoop’s stake gives those plans a Hip-Hop connection beyond a famous face in the stands. He joined Swansea’s ownership group in July 2025, following Croatian soccer star Luka Modric into the Welsh club.

The partnership was built around turning his worldwide audience into business for Swansea. Club officials identified commercial growth as a reason to bring him aboard, with stronger revenue intended to help support a competitive team.

Snoop had already helped introduce Swansea’s home shirt before his investment became official.

That relationship also brought Death Row Records into the club’s orbit through a merchandise collaboration. Gorringe’s November 2025 Business of Sport interview below examined that retail push alongside sponsorship, operating costs and the challenge of competing for promotion.

Snoop’s presence has become part of the stadium itself, where artist Hasan Kamil created a mural marking his arrival.

The club tied his investment to his longstanding interest in soccer, including his earlier work as a FIFA video game ambassador.

Now the rapper is planning another visit to Wales after attending February’s Preston North End match, according to Gorringe.

The executive didn’t announce a date, and the stadium discussion doesn’t establish an approved expansion or construction timetable.

For Snoop, the ownership move added another business to a career already stretching far beyond recording and touring.

His Death Row role connects the venture to a label with its own Hip-Hop history, while Swansea gives that brand a different kind of home crowd.

Swansea’s next stretch after the international break includes West Brom, Middlesbrough and Cardiff City within eight days.

item.title: BREAKING: Yella Beezy Found Guilty Of MO3 Murder, Gets Life Without Parole
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Yella Beezy is convicted of capital murder in MO3's killing and receives life without parole after a Dallas jury's verdict.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy was found guilty of capital murder in MO3’s killing Wednesday and sentenced to life in prison without parole.

The unanimous verdict came in Dallas County after jurors considered the murder-for-hire case against the rapper, who was convicted of capital murder by remuneration.

The jury returned its decision November 11, six years to the day after MO3 was killed on Interstate 35 in Dallas.

Yella Beezy had pleaded not guilty and denied taking part in the killing.

Prosecutors accused him of paying Kewon White to kill MO3. Their case linked the shooting to the rappers’ feud and focused heavily on phone records, witness accounts and a disputed $40,000 cash withdrawal.

The defense challenged those connections throughout the trial. Attorneys argued that the state had asked jurors to fill holes in its evidence and had treated ordinary financial activity as proof of a murder plot.

AllHipHop previously reported on the dispute over the cash, including Dallas Police Detective Eric Barnes’ acknowledgment that investigators could not directly trace recovered money to Yella Beezy’s bank withdrawal.

The transaction took place November 20, 2020, nine days after the shooting. Defense attorney Toby Shook pointed to other large withdrawals and argued that carrying substantial cash was consistent with the rapper’s spending habits.

The defense also challenged testimony about an alleged confession at a South Dallas barbershop. Shook cited cell-tower analysis placing Yella Beezy’s phone roughly 40 miles away in Frisco, while Barnes acknowledged investigators lacked corroborating evidence placing him at the shop.

Closing arguments ended Tuesday. Jurors initially selected a foreperson before being sent home, with deliberations beginning Wednesday morning.

Prosecutor Tommy Adams argued that contacts involving Yella Beezy and Jerry Johnson were followed by calls to White. The defense urged jurors to distinguish those associations from evidence proving the rapper ordered the killing.

Wednesday’s conviction followed a separate capital murder verdict against White, who was sentenced to life in prison in September.

During closing arguments, prosecutors highlighted 15 calls between Johnson and White during Yella Beezy’s 57-hour return trip to North Texas.

item.title: Brandy & Monica Take The Boy Is Mine To Las Vegas For 10 Shows
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Brandy and Monica will bring The Boy Is Mine to Resorts World Las Vegas for 10 performances from May through July 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Brandy and Monica are giving their reunion a Las Vegas address after last year’s arena tour brought them back together onstage. They’ve announced 10 performances of The Boy Is Mine at Resorts World Las Vegas in 2027.

The residency runs from May 29 through July 17 and follows their November 10 appearance on Dancing With the Stars. The pair performed their signature duet during the show’s Grammy-themed episode before announcing their next run together.

Monica hadn’t expected the tour to grow into a residency, according to a statement she shared with Variety. “Originally, it was planned as a one and done, but I’ll be honest, after the first night, I realized it was far deeper,” Monica said.

Brandy had been thinking about that possibility well before the tour began. Back in 2024, she pushed for more collaborations with Monica after they reunited for Ariana Grande’s remix, with touring and a residency among the ideas she raised.

That reunion also put them in Grande’s video, bringing their connection to another generation of listeners. In their June 2025 Tonight Show interview below, they discussed the remix and the joint tour that would follow.

Their original collaboration arrived in 1998 and spent 13 consecutive weeks atop the Billboard Hot 100. The original duet earned both singers the 1999 Grammy for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals.

They later recorded It All Belongs to Me together, giving them another duet between their original hit and the Grande reunion. Their collaboration with Grande brought another Grammy nomination in the Best Pop Duo/Group Performance category.

The move into a residency follows a tour that paired their individual catalogs on the same bill. Kelly Rowland, Muni Long and American Idol winner Jamal Roberts were announced as guests for that 2025 run.

For the new engagement, May 29 and 30 lead into June 2, 4 and 5. The remaining dates fall on July 9, 10, 14, 16 and 17, keeping the entire announced residency within a seven-week stretch.

Black Promoters Collective is producing the new engagement, its first Las Vegas residency.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Guru's Companies Win Legal Fees As Judge Restricts Solar's Lawsuits
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Guru's companies make Solar and his lawyer cover legal costs as a federal judge places limits on another estate fight.
item.content:encoded:
Guru‘s companies are making Solar pay for another federal courtroom fight over the Gang Starr rapper’s legacy.

Solar’s attorney, Emmanuel Coffy, is responsible for the legal bill alongside him.

U.S. District Judge Cathy Seibel imposed the sanctions benefiting Ill Kid Music and Guru Productions. The judge found that Solar and Coffy pursued previously rejected claims in bad faith. “As such, his claims are without color,” Seibel wrote of Solar.

“It is hard to fathom any reason other than harassment for Mr. Coffy filing plainly precluded claims,” Seibel wrote. The ruling makes both men jointly responsible for the companies’ attorneys’ fees.

Solar must also get the court’s permission before pursuing specified Guru estate claims in the Southern District of New York. That restriction reaches trademarks, company ownership and related royalties, while similar New York state filings must include the order.

AllHipHop’s coverage traced the public feud to Guru’s hospitalization before his April 2010 death. His nephew accused Solar of blocking relatives’ access, while Solar denied that and said family members had visited.

The family later challenged a purported final letter that praised Solar and distanced Guru from Premier. Relatives said Guru never regained consciousness after entering a coma, while Solar insisted the statement came directly from him.

By 2021, the estate was accusing Solar of concealing assets, including proceeds from unreleased recordings. That complaint pushed the dispute beyond song credits into efforts to collect money the estate said he owed.

A 2014 estate ruling rejected Solar’s asserted ownership of the companies and trademarks, but the appeal wasn’t a complete defeat. The appellate court left those ownership findings intact while overturning other findings concerning certain creative works and reducing the repayment ordered against him.

Solar then sued Premier and the companies again in 2025, seeking damages and restrictions on disputed material.

He voluntarily dropped that lawsuit in December, but the companies continued seeking sanctions afterward. Their fee records are due November 13, and the judge hasn’t fixed a dollar amount.

Solar and Coffy have until November 27 to challenge only the reasonableness of the requested legal fees.

item.title: Hip Hop Beauty Gives Texas Southern Students A Marketplace Of Their Own
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Hip Hop Beauty pairs its Houston photo exhibition with a sales event for TSU entrepreneurs and classes led by industry pros.
item.content:encoded:
Hip Hop Beauty is bringing student-run businesses into the picture when its traveling exhibition reaches Texas Southern University this week.

Erykah Badu appears in the project’s collection through photographer Keith Major’s work. The broader venture makes photography available to collectors while pairing art with beauty services and conversations about the people behind the images.

The November 12-20 Houston exhibition includes a November 20 student marketplace, organizers announced.

“The Jesse H. Jones School of Business, the College of Liberal Arts and Behavioral Sciences, and all of our partners are beyond excited to partner with Hip Hop Beauty Circa 1973 during Entrepreneurship Week at TSU,” associate dean Dr. Michon Benson said in a statement. “Thembisa S. Mshaka and Ashunta Sheriff-Kendricks are the kinds of real-world experts who will encourage and inspire our students.”

The project comes from makeup artist Ashunta Sheriff-Kendricks and author Thembisa S. Mshaka. Its earlier New York Fashion Week presentation opened at Studio6 Gallery in February with photography by Major, Stacy Gray and Mazi Smazi. That stop paired the exhibition with a panel moderated by Jamila Mustafa.

Texas Southern has also been part of an Interscope initiative connecting HBCU students with the music business. That 2024 program included campus pop-ups, school-specific artwork and merchandise, with a donation to the university for each related item sold. Howard and Tennessee State were part of the same opening group.

The Hip Hop Beauty Market runs November 20 from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. in the C.S. Lane Building.
